audits.title: Audit of cancer pain management in a cancer centre.
audits.setting: Two teaching hospitals of the Nottingham Cancer Centre

cycle1.result: Of 186 patients, 52 had cancer pain and 47 assessed; more than half had unrelieved pain that was severe at worst.

audits.other_findings: Uncontrolled pain was associated with no formal assessment, no pain-care plan and not being seen by the palliative care team.
audits.citation: Menzies K, Murray J, Wilcock A. Audit of cancer pain management in a cancer centre. Int J Palliat Nurs. 2000;6(9):443-447. doi:10.12968/ijpn.2000.6.9.9056. PMID: 12388896.

audits.title: Cancer pain management in Lanarkshire: a community-based audit.
audits.standard: Scottish Cancer Pain Audit prescribing standards

cycle1.result: Pain scores recorded in 90% of 3259 visits; specific gaps in prescribing identified; 88% of practices submitted forms.

audits.intervention: Results fed back to prescribers and used for a primary care education programme
audits.other_findings: Continuous audit was achievable within normal care; stakeholder engagement was key.
audits.citation: Oxenham D, Duncan R, Fischbacher M. Cancer pain management in Lanarkshire: a community-based audit. Palliat Med. 2003;17(8):708-713. doi:10.1191/0269216303pm840oa. PMID: 14694923.

audits.title: Implementation of cancer pain guidelines by acute care nurse practitioners using an audit and feedback strategy.
audits.setting: Acute care nurse practitioners, Norris Cotton Cancer Center, Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center (inpatients)

cycle1.result: Baseline group of 96 patients completed the Brief Pain Inventory; adherence figures not reported in abstract.

audits.intervention: Audit and feedback: nurse practitioners received weekly feedback on pain scores and guideline adherence.

cycle2.result: Nurse practitioner adherence to guidelines increased during audit and feedback; pain intensity did not differ significantly between groups.

audits.other_findings: Intervention group patients reported significantly less overall pain interference. Eight nurse practitioners took part.
audits.citation: Dulko D, Hertz E, Julien J, Beck S, Mooney K. Implementation of cancer pain guidelines by acute care nurse practitioners using an audit and feedback strategy. J Am Acad Nurse Pract. 2010;22(1):45-55. doi:10.1111/j.1745-7599.2009.00469.x. PMID: 20074196.

audits.title: [Improving the quality of cancer pain management in palliative care unit: Targeted clinical audit].
audits.standard: 19-item audit grid based on pilot committee recommendations
audits.setting: Palliative care unit, Hospices civils de Lyon
audits.intervention: Corrective measures proposed after T1 (details not given in the abstract).
audits.other_findings: 60 consecutive patients over the two periods; patient education and record documentation still needed improvement.

audits.title: Screening and Audit as Service-Level Strategies to Support Implementation of Australian Guidelines for Cancer Pain Management in Adults: A Feasibility Study.
audits.standard: Australian guidelines for cancer pain management; feasibility thresholds of 75% screening and median 30 minutes per audit
audits.setting: One oncology outpatient service and one palliative care outpatient and inpatient service, Sydney

cycle1.result: 95% (n = 429) of 452 visits screened; median audit time 37.5 minutes (31 records); adherence to indicators ranged from 63% (pain assessment at first presentation) to 94% (regular pain assessment and regular medication).

audits.other_findings: Electronic pain screening was technically challenging and time-intensive for nurses.
audits.citation: Lovell M, Birch MR, Luckett T, Phillips J, Davidson PM, Agar M, et al.. Screening and Audit as Service-Level Strategies to Support Implementation of Australian Guidelines for Cancer Pain Management in Adults: A Feasibility Study. Pain Manag Nurs. 2019;20(2):113-117. doi:10.1016/j.pmn.2018.05.004. PMID: 30448191.

audits.title: Audit of cancer pain management practices at the adult oncology center, University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia.
audits.setting: Adult oncology ward, University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with ESMO guidelines 55.46%; pain assessed with NRS in 100%; subcutaneous route first choice in only 2 (1.16%) unable to take oral opioids.

audits.other_findings: Regular training programme on cancer pain management recommended.
audits.citation: Asmare TB, Tawuye HY, Tegegne BA, Gobezie NZ, Wubet HB, Gedefaw GD, et al.. Audit of cancer pain management practices at the adult oncology center, University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia. Front Oncol. 2025;15:1542227. doi:10.3389/fonc.2025.1542227. PMID: 40386556.

audits.title: An audit into the knowledge of pain control among medical staff in a Ugandan teaching hospital
audits.standard: Eight audit standards on pain control knowledge
audits.setting: Medical department, Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline knowledge showed deficiencies in a number of areas.

audits.intervention: Education programme for doctors and students.

cycle2.result: Knowledge improved universally; correct prescriptions increased only slightly.

audits.other_findings: Education alone did little to change prescribing.
audits.citation: Royston R, Morgan W. An audit into the knowledge of pain control among medical staff in a Ugandan teaching hospital. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2012;2(Suppl 1):A74.1-A74. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2012-000196.215.
